framework.summary: Large frontier developers must write, implement, follow and publish a frontier AI framework within one year of enactment or 90 days of qualifying, and review it at least annually.
framework.quote: a large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on a publicly available website of such developer a frontier AI framework

transparency_report.summary: Before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, the developer must publish a report on the model, including its catastrophic-risk assessments and results.
transparency_report.quote: the frontier developer of such model shall publish on a publicly available website of such developer a report on such model

incident_reporting.summary: A frontier developer must report a critical safety incident to the Under Secretary of Commerce within 72 hours of learning facts that establish a reasonable belief it occurred.
incident_reporting.quote: not later than 72 hours after a frontier developer learns facts sufficient to establish a reasonable belief that a critical safety incident has occurred with respect to a frontier model of such developer, such developer shall submit

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury must be reported to a law enforcement agency within 24 hours of discovery.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: Not later than 24 hours after a frontier developer discovers a critical safety incident that poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, such developer shall report such incident to a law enforcement agency

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must hire a third party for an annual independent audit of compliance with their framework; the largest developers must also retain a licensed independent verification organization.
third_party_audit.quote: a large frontier developer shall retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the frontier AI framework of such developer

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee whistleblower protections.

registration.summary: A large frontier developer may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier model without a current disclosure statement filed with the Under Secretary and the fee paid.
registration.quote: a large frontier developer may not develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part, without a current disclosure statement filed with the Under Secretary

shutdown.summary: The Secretary of Commerce may order a developer's development, deployment or internal use of a frontier model suspended or restricted on a finding of imminent catastrophic risk; developers need not build a kill switch.
shutdown.quote: The Secretary may issue an emergency order suspending or restricting a frontier developer's development, deployment, or internal use of a frontier model upon finding

compute_threshold.summary: A frontier model is a foundation model trained with more than 10^26 operations, including later fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; the Under Secretary may raise the figure.
compute_threshold.quote: a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large frontier developer, with its affiliates over 36 months, has gross revenues over $50,000,000 and at least $1,000,000,000 in AI development spending; a very large one has over $5,000,000,000 and at least $10,000,000,000.
revenue_threshold.quote: had gross revenues in excess of $50,000,000

harm_threshold.summary: Catastrophic risk is a risk of death or serious injury to more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in property damage, from a single incident involving a frontier model.
harm_threshold.quote: will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people, or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss of, property

penalties.summary: Up to $1,000,000 per violation (each day separate); $10,000 a day for no disclosure statement; up to $10,000,000 for breaking an emergency order (willful breach is criminal). Attorney General enforces.
penalties.quote: A frontier developer that violates this section shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than $1,000,000 per violation.

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; deadlines run from enactment.

notes: Very large developers must retain a licensed IVO (Sec. 5(b)) with reports at least every 6 months. Sec. 9 (state-law preemption, text not fully read past its definitions) was not summarized. Sec. 4(h) incident reports are made to the Under Secretary, imminent-risk reports to law enforcement. Bill is a preemption and licensing-regime design; owner should review Sec. 9.
